races.name: Follow Tote On X Claiming Race

runners_data.name: Taj Crown
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for K J Condon and W J Lee, ran on Good last time out just 7 days ago and the trip looks within range; visor (v) headgear worn, trainer 1 from 8 in 14-day window, but recent form figures of 9-5-2-8-6 suggest inconsistency and he rarely wins even when placed.

runners_data.name: Persian Bliss
runners_data.note: Denis Gerard Hogan runner back after a 116-day absence (tongue-tie, has worn tp headgear), previously placed over 18f on Good ground suggesting stamina is not an issue; the long absence and poor sim-going record of 0 wins and 0 places from 10 runs on Good are significant flags.

runners_data.name: Royal Approval
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's confirmed pace-setter who gets a clear lead here; STYLE_FIT tag of 0.93 acknowledges this position is slightly out of its typical role, but in this field it is the natural leader — last won over 10f on Soft and jumps form suggests it can stay, though 376 days off the track is a major concern.

runners_data.name: Plontier
runners_data.note: W P Mullins' veteran nine-year-old hold-up horse returning after 282 days off (208 days jump-adjusted), with a weak sim-going record of 0 from 12 on Good; the Mullins yard angle is always worth noting but this horse has been running down the field in similar conditions.

runners_data.name: Battling Siki
runners_data.note: Mark Fahey's four-year-old ran 60 days ago and wore a hood (p) in recent starts; form figures are modest (7-4-5-9) but all runs are at a similar level and the 60-day absence is not alarming — interesting each-way profile for a hold-up type given the pace scenario, though style fit is compromised.

runners_data.name: Timandi
runners_data.note: James Barrett runner that is a genuine deep closer in terms of true running style, though the race shape pushes it forward on the map — its natural inclination to come from the rear means it races out of role here and the STYLE_FIT of 0.90 is a fair reflection; five runs without a win and poor form figures (-5-0-0-9-4) offer little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Stone Rulya
runners_data.note: Eoin Doyle's four-year-old returns after 263 days (5 jump-adjusted) and carries a noted tendency to fade in the finish, which is a material concern in a race where it is already being mapped away from its natural trailing position; the 0-from-9 sim-going record and consistent finishing positions in double figures make this hard to support.

runners_data.name: Wolfpack
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's second runner in the race, a true hold-up type whose natural finishing inclination is being constrained by the race shape; also tagged as one who fades in the finish and has a sim-going record of 1 win but only 1 place from 11 on Good — the Elliott yard is in strong form (T14: 12/57) which is the one positive angle to note.

races.paceDynamic: Royal Approval is the confirmed lone front-runner here, and with no genuine challenger for the lead on early pace, Leigh Roche can dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on a Good surface over 1m4f at Tramore. Taj Crown and Persian Bliss are the other prominent-style runners who will look to track close to the pace, meaning the first three positions in the early stages are effectively already allocated among those three. The field nominally contains several hold-up types — Wolfpack, Stone Rulya, and Timandi — but all three are true deep closers who have been mapped forward on the race shape diagram simply because the rear of the field is overcrowded; in reality they are unlikely to get the prominent berths that would suit them, and their STYLE_FIT discounts reflect genuine racing-out-of-role risk. A lone front-runner setting a measured gallop on Good ground over this trip at a tight track like Tramore creates a race that strongly favours prominent racers who can travel in behind the leader and pounce entering the straight, rather than horses asked to make up ground from deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls Race
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Approval dictates an uncontested, measured gallop throughout and the field never applies meaningful pressure.
scenarios.body: Royal Approval establishes a rhythm from the front with no rival willing to go with it, and Leigh Roche can conserve energy through the middle section before extending in the straight. Prominent trackers Taj Crown and Persian Bliss, sitting just off the pace, are ideally placed to pounce if Royal Approval fades late but struggle to pass it if it has dictated entirely on its own terms.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Approval sets a genuine pace that takes its toll approaching the final two furlongs and a close-tracking prominent runner sweeps past.
scenarios.body: Taj Crown or Persian Bliss, travelling smoothly in the slipstream, picks off a tiring Royal Approval as the race enters its final stages on the tight Tramore circuit. This shape suits horses who can race within themselves while on the pace and produce a clean finish rather than a sustained closing run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Breaks Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace genuinely quickens early and the leaders burn each other out, giving a held-up runner a genuine target.
scenarios.body: Plontier, the most experienced hold-up horse in the field trained by W P Mullins, would be best placed to benefit from a genuinely run race where stamina becomes the deciding factor in the closing stages. However, this scenario requires conditions that are unlikely given Royal Approval has no pace rival to force it into a truly fast gallop, and the redistributed closers Wolfpack, Stone Rulya, and Timandi all carry style-fit concerns that reduce their probability here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Messy Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so slow that the field concertinas and the race turns into a sprint finish from two out.
scenarios.body: A crawl from Royal Approval compresses the field and negates tactical advantages, turning the race into a test of raw speed over the final furlong where horses that handle Tramore's tight turns and have a sharp finishing kick hold the edge. This is the least likely shape given the distance and the number of hold-up horses who will be anxious to be making ground, creating at least some natural pressure on the pace.

watchPoints.text: Royal Approval has been off the track for 376 days — watch the market closely, as any drift in price would suggest connections are uncertain about its readiness to front-run effectively after such a lengthy absence.

Wolfpack and Stone Rulya both carry "fades in finish" flags and are already racing out of their natural hold-up roles — if either is seen niggled at or losing position before the straight, they are unlikely to land a blow.
Persian Bliss returns from 116 days off for Denis Gerard Hogan and has a 0-from-10 record on Good ground in similar going — watch the paddock for signs of fitness given the extended break.

With three redistributed hold-up horses (Wolfpack, Stone Rulya, Timandi) all likely to settle further back than the map shows, watch whether any of them attempts to force its way forward at the start, which could briefly disrupt the early pace and give Royal Approval an even cleaner lead.

Taj Crown wore a visor last time and ran 7 days ago — watch whether W J Lee tracks Royal Approval immediately from the jump or allows a gap to form, as the tactical call in the first half-mile could define whether the prominent-tracker scenario plays out.

races.name: Waterford Castle And Resort Style Evening August 15th Maiden

runners_data.name: Big Dispute
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with course-relevant form at 16-18f trips, goes well on Good; Rory Cleary takes over and the trainer has been quiet lately — by nature a hold-up horse, though the crowded rear means he may end up racing closer to midfield than ideal, tempering confidence in a late finish.|

runners_data.name: Double Indian
runners_data.note: Mrs Harrington's four-year-old has only two runs on record, both on Good, and fades in the finish — a natural closer squeezed out of the back group by sheer numbers, so the redistribution to midfield suits neither his style nor his stamina profile over this trip.|

runners_data.name: El Galvino
runners_data.note: 144 days off the track and all recent starts came on Flat/Standard surfaces rather than turf, making the going switch a genuine concern; a hold-up runner by inclination, the crowded rear forces him wider in the field, and the form figures on similar ground (0W0P from six) don't inspire.|

runners_data.name: Half Cut
runners_data.note: Sole run was a modest 15th of a field on Good over 12f, giving little to work with; the fades-in-finish warning compounds the uncertainty, and Anthony Mullins has had limited recent winners with this horse.|

runners_data.name: Jetoile
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old veteran who has won over 20f on Good and brings clear front-running credentials — Colin Keane's booking is significant and the headgear (tp) suggests connections are trying to sharpen him up; the uncontested lead is his to take, making this the pivotal runner in shaping the entire race.|

runners_data.name: Way Down South
runners_data.note: Won over 20f on Soft and has placed at 19-22f, suggesting the 1m4f trip here may be on the short side, but W J Lee gives confidence and a prominent style means he should track Jetoile closely throughout.|

runners_data.name: Blue Nasturtium
runners_data.note: Lightly raced four-year-old for K J Condon with no going data available and an unknown style — Donagh O'Connor rides and the trainer has had recent winners, but the unknowns here are significant and must be treated with caution.|

runners_data.name: Dream On Baby
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who has placed at 20-24f distances consistently, including a win over 21f on Good; Gary Carroll partners a horse who prefers prominent racing, and the longer recent absence (271 days with a jumps break) is the main concern, though two trainer winners from 11 in 14 days suggests the yard is in form.|

runners_data.name: Kimy
runners_data.note: Multiple fade-in-finish flags across five runs, including two poor efforts over 20f on Good; Nicola Burns (5lb claim) takes over for Thomas Mullins, but the form figures of 07 in recent outings and a consistent inability to sustain an effort make this a difficult one to support.|

runners_data.name: Walls Cross
runners_data.note: Single run on Polytrack/Heathpark gives no turf or Good-ground reference point — Timothy Doyle's four-year-old is an unknown quantity on this surface, and Leigh Roche will need to educate rather than exploit on debut turf ground.|

races.paceDynamic: Jetoile is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Colin Keane aboard, will likely stride into an uncontested lead from the outset over this 1m4f trip on Good ground at Tramore. Way Down South and Dream On Baby are the most likely prominent challengers to track Jetoile through the early stages, but neither figures to seriously pressure the pace, meaning Jetoile can control tempo entirely on their own terms. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Big Dispute, Double Indian, and El Galvino are all genuine closers by nature but are mapped to midfield given the crowding at the back; of the three, Big Dispute (Rory Cleary, solid form at the trip) is the most likely to actually secure a rearward position with any purpose. A solo, uncontested lead at a sustainable gallop on a flat course strongly favours front-running and prominent profiles who can dictate and control the race from the front, with hold-up runners facing a diminished closing opportunity if the pace is never truly strong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jetoile Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Jetoile leads at a controlled, unchallenged gallop and the prominent duo cannot close the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: Jetoile settles into a rhythm with no rival willing to race alongside, conserving energy for a sustained run to the line; this shape rewards horses racing on or near the pace who can quicken off a steady gallop in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Reel In Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Way Down South or Dream On Baby track Jetoile closely and wear them down in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A slightly stronger tempo, encouraged by Way Down South pressing from second, sets up a finish between the lead and prominent horses; Dream On Baby's consistent placed form at this type of trip makes it a key threat in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Sweeps Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight and a horse racing in mid-division picks up the pieces.
scenarios.body: A falsely run race where front-runners tie up opens the race for a horse like Big Dispute, who has the form to sustain a run from midfield; his most recent run at 9f/GOO hints he's capable when the race falls right, even if racing somewhat out of natural role here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Genuine Closer Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the field strings out, allowing a true hold-up horse to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: With multiple redistributed closers unable to fully slot into their preferred rear position, a genuine late run is the least likely outcome in this pace-light scenario; Double Indian's fade-in-finish flag and Half Cut's lone run profile make this a low-probability shape.

watchPoints.text: Jetoile's ability to control tempo entirely unchallenged is the single biggest race-shaping factor — if Colin Keane dictates a slow early pace, the entire field is compromised and hold-up horses like Big Dispute and Double Indian will find the straight far too short to mount a meaningful challenge.

Dream On Baby returns from 271 days off (with a jumps break) and connections must have this horse ready — monitor paddock condition and early market moves, as a fit Emmet Mullins runner with that consistent placed form could be underestimated at a price.

Big Dispute, Double Indian, and El Galvino are all genuine closers by inclination but none can fully drop to the rear in this shape — watch whether any of them are ridden handier than usual, as the jockeys may adapt early, which would materially change how the finish unfolds.

Blue Nasturtium is a complete unknown — lightly raced, no going record, style unclassified — and K J Condon's yard has had recent winners; a drifting or shortening price in the market is the only guide available before the off.

Way Down South's best form has come at 19-24f trips, notably on Soft ground; if the 1m4f distance proves sharp enough to prevent him sustaining his usual prominent effort all the way, his influence as Jetoile's closest pursuer may fade well before the line.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Handicap

runners_data.name: Kashel Spring
runners_data.note: Long absent (268 days) which is a significant concern, but this 4yo has similar-going form at 12f Good (2 wins, 2 places) and jockey Alan Casey's claim reduces weight; genuine hold-up style will need a strong pace to aim at, which this shape may not provide.

runners_data.name: Sea Coral
runners_data.note: Tagged with a finishing fade flag which is a structural worry in a slowly-run race; has placed twice at 12f on Good but steps up to 1m4f and races from the back, meaning she needs Daboya to set genuine fractions to have any chance of getting competitive.

runners_data.name: Marmeladova
runners_data.note: Won over 10f Good just 15 days ago in sharp form for K J Condon, but her natural hold-up racing style places her further back than the map shows — she is being pushed closer than ideal and the STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence, even though her OR and recent win make her one of the more interesting form entries.

runners_data.name: Daboya
runners_data.note: The one confirmed pace-setter and the pivotal horse in this race; Colin Keane is a major asset, she has won at 13f and 16f on Good, and wearing blinkers (hg:b) sharpens her early resolution — the uncontested lead is hers to lose.

runners_data.name: Justenzia
runners_data.note: Has placed twice in recent 13f and 10f Good ground starts for the Hogan stable, but OR 70 and a true hold-up profile mean she is compromised by this race shape; racing closer than natural per the redistribution, her STYLE_FIT discount is justified.

runners_data.name: La Dame Blanche
runners_data.note: A 7yo whose best Tramore-relevant form shows a 3rd at 16f Good and a 4th at 12f Good, but she has gone 0 from 11 in similar going; another genuine hold-up type forced to track closer than preferred, limiting her scope for a winning late challenge.

runners_data.name: Questionable
runners_data.note: Returning from 299 days off (93 days with a Flat jockey switch noted) and racing over a longer trip than her recent 10f form — the layoff alone is a significant flag, and her natural closing style is further compromised by the pace map redistribution.

races.paceDynamic: Daboya is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with Colin Keane aboard, will stride into an uncontested lead from the off over this 1m4f trip at Tramore. With no rival capable of or likely to seriously challenge for the early lead, Daboya sets a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good ground — neither dawdling nor injecting enough pace to blow the field apart, but dictating every yard at a tempo entirely of her own choosing. Behind her, the remainder of the field is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up types — Marmeladova, Justenzia, La Dame Blanche and Questionable are all genuine closers who have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because the field holds far more hold-up horses than can realistically race from the rear in a seven-runner contest; of these, Marmeladova, with her superior OR and form, is most likely to secure the best midfield position, while Justenzia and La Dame Blanche will be forced slightly closer than ideal. This race shape — a lone, unhurried front-runner setting a fair but unspectacular gallop on quick ground — strongly favours a horse with tactical versatility or proven ability to travel prominently and quicken, not pure hold-up horses waiting on a strong pace injection that may never come.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Daboya Controls, Converts
scenarios.trigger: If Daboya leads unchallenged and Keane manages the gallop to neutralise late closers on Good ground.
scenarios.body: Daboya sets fractions she is comfortable with, never putting the race to bed too early but arriving at the straight with petrol in the tank; a horse who has already won over this distance at Good to Firm and recorded recent form at 13f Good is ideally set up to hold on. Prominent or close-tracking runners will benefit most, as the measured tempo gives hold-up horses no momentum-generating pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Daboya goes too slowly and a strong late surge from the best-placed hold-up horse overwhelms her in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A falsely slow early gallop can compress the race into a sprint finish, and while this theoretically suits closers, the reality is that this field's genuine hold-up horses are racing closer than natural — their finishing kick may be blunted by having to cover more ground mid-race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pressing Move Upends Leader
scenarios.trigger: If a redistributed prominent horse moves to pressurise Daboya from the halfway point, forcing a contested pace that opens the race up.
scenarios.body: Should a rival press Keane's mount turning for home, Daboya's stamina reserves are tested and her lead narrows; a horse with the best turn of foot or highest RPR becomes the beneficiary of the resulting pace duel.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Scrappy Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed hold-up group causes interference or traffic problems in the straight, scrambling the outcome.
scenarios.body: With five horses effectively racing closer than their natural style dictates, congestion in the straight is a real risk; the horse with the clearest run and the widest position in the straight benefits most.

watchPoints.text: Daboya — if Colin Keane is unable to secure the early lead or is pushed wider than ideal leaving the stalls, the entire race shape unravels and the value in backing any pace-dependent scenario evaporates.

Marmeladova — watch how far off the pace W J Lee settles her in the first half-mile; if she is forced to race closer than her natural style through circumstance rather than choice, her finishing effort may arrive too soon.

Sea Coral — the finishing-fade flag is critical to monitor in running; if she is still travelling at the two-furlong pole she may be a serious threat, but any sign of laboured movement before that point confirms she is not staying the 1m4f trip.

Kashel Spring — a 268-day absence warrants a watch on how she moves in the parade ring and early in the race; if she travels smoothly tracking the pace her fitness may be sufficient, but any signs of greenness after such a break can be dismissed quickly.

La Dame Blanche — Gary Carroll may attempt to use the small field to find a clean position on the outside rather than being hemmed in; watch her track position in the first three furlongs as it will determine whether she has any realistic chance of making her closing run count.

races.name: Tote Tramore Derby Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Brewel Hill
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who has shown decent form on good ground at around 10f, though today's step up to 1m4f is an interesting test; 282 days off is a major concern and Peter McCreery's yard has had no recent activity, making it hard to trust at a big price fresh.

runners_data.name: Chopsticks
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner with a realistic chance of dictating entirely; Paddy Harnett (5) rides and John McConnell's yard shows a T14 of 0/22, so trainer form is subdued, but the tactical advantage of leading a hold-up-dominated field on good ground is significant — the [STYLE_FIT=0.91] tag notes this is out of typical role so discount if pace turns genuinely hot.

runners_data.name: Churchwarden
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead has been in strong form (T14: 9/36) and Gary Carroll is an astute booking; a hold-up type by profile but has placed on good ground and the step back from soft should help — the layoff of 57 days (32 since joining) is manageable with this trainer.

runners_data.name: Magna Gee Gee
runners_data.note: A four-year-old hold-up type with no wins or places on good going in five attempts on similar ground; W J Lee is a quality jockey but form figures of 07086 offer little encouragement and the trip is longer than anything she has handled with distinction.

runners_data.name: Vervain
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a win at 12f on good ground in her best effort; flagged as a true hold-up runner mapped to midfield due to congestion at the rear, and also tagged ⚠ for fading in finishes — her 259-day absence is a major fitness concern, and discount her chance in a shape where she cannot get her favoured late position.

runners_data.name: Surviving Murmansk
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old with a win at 16f on good ground in his career-best, but 228 days off (38 since joining trainer James Barcoe) is a serious question mark; genuinely needs to come from behind but the race map has him placed in midfield because of overcrowding — his true efficacy depends on others going hard early, which Chopsticks is unlikely to do.

runners_data.name: Highway Sixty One
runners_data.note: Consistent placed form at 12f on good and standard surfaces for a young four-year-old, running just 25 days ago which is a fitness positive; however, a genuine hold-up runner whose map position in midfield reflects field congestion rather than natural style — will need to find a way back from the pack in a slowly-run race.

runners_data.name: Itsalonglongroad
runners_data.note: A 12-year-old veteran with excellent course-distance stamina at 16f on good ground (four places from 15 similar-ground runs); visored for the first time today which is a flag, and naturally races from the rear — mapped in midfield only because hold-up slots are full, so his chance hinges on getting his true position at the back and the pace being strong enough to reel in.

runners_data.name: Plus Or Minus
runners_data.note: A four-year-old with a poor recent string of form figures (8790-7) and only two runs on good ground offering limited encouragement; wears a tongue-tie, is flagged for fading finishes, and is a true hold-up horse racing in a shape where the gentle pace will not set him up — the midfield map position reflects field congestion, not his preferred racing style.

runners_data.name: Appian Way
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old veteran who has consistently finished mid-division on good ground in staying trips up to 22-24f, making today's 1m4f well short of his best trip; hold-up type racing against the grain of the pace shape and flagged for fading finishes — 146 days off (32 since trainer switch) adds further risk.

runners_data.name: Fantasy Fara
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a poor form string (900-00) and all recent runs at shorter distances of 10f on soft or heavy — the good ground and step to 1m4f are both against her, and a tongue-tie is worn; true hold-up type whose midfield map placement is a function of field congestion rather than natural inclination.

runners_data.name: Shakita
runners_data.note: A four-year-old with limited staying form, having finished 10th-17th in recent runs over various trips; wears no headgear and has modest form on good going — a natural hold-up runner placed in midfield on the map only because the rear of the field is overpopulated, and current form offers no basis for confidence.

runners_data.name: Jazz Forever
runners_data.note: Ran just four days ago which is an aggressive turnaround, and the visored hold-up horse is flagged for fading in finishes; best effort was a third at 13f on good ground, so the trip is not an issue, but the quick return and tendency to weaken late makes this a difficult race to trust him in.

races.paceDynamic: Chopsticks is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 13-runner field and will set out to lead from the front, establishing an uncontested, controlled gallop on good ground over 1m4f at Tramore. With no genuine rival willing or able to challenge for the early lead, Paddy Harnett's mount can dictate a sustainable, even tempo that plays directly into the hands of those able to track closely. The remainder of this field is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up types — Vervain, Surviving Murmansk, Itsalonglongroad, Highway Sixty One, Plus Or Minus, and others are all natural rear-runners redistributed to midfield on the map because there simply is not room for all of them to settle at the back; in reality, several will find themselves racing wide or further back than ideal. A single front-runner setting a comfortable pace on good turf over this stamina-oriented trip favours prominent and close-tracking runners who can latch onto Chopsticks' back early and have something left in the tank when the tempo lifts turning for home — true hold-up horses dependent on a strong early gallop to deliver a late run will find the fractions too gentle to generate meaningful momentum.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Chopsticks Leads, Trackers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Chopsticks dictates a sedate, uncontested pace and a close tracker is able to sit within two lengths throughout before asserting in the straight.
scenarios.body: Chopsticks sets the fractions entirely to suit himself, and any runner able to position prominently behind him gets a dream stalking position into the home turn; the good ground and flat track mean the winner is likely to emerge from the first three or four in the run from the two-furlong pole.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Chopsticks Wins Wire To Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays genuinely modest and no prominent rival has the class or energy to reel Chopsticks in during the straight.
scenarios.body: With an uncontested lead and a comfortable rhythm, Chopsticks could simply steal an unassailable break turning for home on the flat track; John McConnell's yard is in form on a T14 strike-rate of 0/22 but the horse has shown front-running ability previously and can capitalise if the field settles too far back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If Chopsticks' pace is genuinely slow enough to compress the field into a bunch, causing a chaotic home straight where one of the deeper hold-up runners finds a gap and pounces.
scenarios.body: A bunched race at this distance on flat ground can produce a big finish from the rear, but most of the true hold-up types here have been redistributed on the map because they cannot all get their natural position, reducing their chance of delivering a clean late run; runners like Surviving Murmansk and Itsalonglongroad would need everything to fall perfectly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Reigns
scenarios.trigger: If a significant number of the redistributed hold-up horses jostle for position early, creating a bungled tactical race with no clear early shape.
scenarios.body: With 13 runners and only one true front-runner, a scrambled mid-race order could produce an unpredictable result, but this field lacks the class or the genuine early pace to create the kind of pressure that typically scrambles form; the most likely beneficiary remains a horse that finds daylight close to the pace.

watchPoints.text: Churchwarden is the primary tracking danger — Henry De Bromhead's strong form (T14: 9/36) combined with Gary Carroll could see him latch onto Chopsticks' back from the outset and deliver the decisive move turning for home.

Chopsticks' effective pace advantage could evaporate quickly if Paddy Harnett misjudges the tempo — watch whether he bowls along freely or if any of the redistributed hold-up horses scramble early to claim a prominent berth ahead of him.
Jazz Forever's four-day turnaround is unusually quick and bears watching in the market; if support comes despite the quick return it may signal the trainer has a specific reason for running fresh.

Surviving Murmansk and Itsalonglongroad are both true hold-up veterans with good staying form on good ground — watch whether they can find their natural rear position or are forced wide and into midfield by the congested field, as their finishing runs depend entirely on getting a clear passage.

Brewel Hill's 282-day absence for Peter McCreery (T14: 0/0) is one of the race's biggest unknowns — any significant market move late would upgrade his relevance significantly given his prior good-ground form.

races.name: Tramoreraces.ie Handicap

runners_data.name: Soaring Sun
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter here; Good-ground record is modest (0 wins, 0 places from 2 comparable runs) but the role suits this race shape and Patrick Flynn's 1/4 recent strike rate gives mild support — the STYLE_FIT tag reflects it is racing slightly out of role but the lack of any rival for the lead makes that irrelevant today.

runners_data.name: Showyoutheropes
runners_data.note: Best comparable form of any closer in this field — 1 win and 4 places from 8 Good-ground runs — and Gary Carroll's presence on a 109-day returner for O'Leary is the key watch; the layoff is the one concern but the form pattern fits a hold-up horse in a race like this.

runners_data.name: Devine Genius
runners_data.note: Eleven-day turnaround for a horse whose recent form reads 13th, 11th, 6th on Good ground, and the ⚠ fade flag is damning over 1m4f; Adam Browne-Souza's 7lb claim does not compensate for a horse that repeatedly stops in the finish.

runners_data.name: Metamorphic
runners_data.note: Harrington's yard is firing (5/30 in 14 days) but Metamorphic has posted three nines in recent form and has not placed on Good or Standard ground across five runs; the headgear (tongue-tie and pad) and trainer form keep it from being dismissed entirely.

runners_data.name: Glendower
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse by inclination yet the crowded rear means it is likely to race closer to midfield than ideal; five places from 15 Good-ground runs show it stays involved without winning, and the ht headgear adds a layer of unpredictability.

runners_data.name: Guy's Girl
runners_data.note: W J Lee takes the ride for McCreery on a mare whose best recent run was 3rd over 13f on Good — directly relevant — yet she is a true hold-up type forced wider in the field than she would like; that positional compromise limits her upside.

runners_data.name: Eastern Blue Bird
runners_data.note: Wears a visor, has not finished in the first eight in any of the last five starts, and the ⚠ fade flag over 14f on Good makes this a difficult profile to support regardless of where she ends up in the field; form reads 8-8-9-13-11 in the last five.

runners_data.name: Forlio
runners_data.note: Colin Keane's booking is the single most compelling angle in this race for a horse whose 4th over 11f on Good last time is quietly solid; a true hold-up type carrying the p headgear, mapped to midfield, but Keane's ability to manufacture a position from anywhere is a genuine offset.

runners_data.name: Miss Crinshawn
runners_data.note: Ben Coen partners a filly whose last five starts show a 4th, 2nd (Heavy), 4th, 3rd and 10th — consistent without winning — and the 13f Good form (4th) is directly applicable; pushed into midfield rather than the deep rear, she may actually benefit from a slightly more prominent berth than her natural style.

runners_data.name: Oust
runners_data.note: Three-year-old carrying 134lbs but the OR=72 top weight and Good-ground record of 0W/2P from 6 runs suggest a horse that competes without winning; racing just off Soaring Sun is the obvious tactic for Rory Cleary and this shape gives it a clear route to a place.

runners_data.name: A Pretty Penny
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Good ground recently (1 win from 4 Good-ground runs) and the 3yo allowance at 121lbs is meaningful in a handicap like this; Julian Pietropaolo's 7lb claim and a trainer with no recent runners (T14:0/0) suggests limited live support, but the weight is a real asset if she can settle from the rear.

races.paceDynamic: Soaring Sun and Oust are the only two horses with any realistic claim to forward positions, creating a thin pace facade in what is otherwise a deeply hold-up dominated field of 11. Soaring Sun has one confirmed front-running run on record and is expected to go forward and control the tempo, with Oust likely to track closely in second; between them they will set a measured, uncontested gallop over the 1m4f trip on Good turf — nothing extravagant, nothing suicidal. The overwhelming majority of this field — Showyoutheropes, Glendower, Guy's Girl, Eastern Blue Bird, Forlio, Miss Crinshawn, A Pretty Penny, Devine Genius and Metamorphic — are genuine hold-up types who will be anchored in the rear half, creating a bunched, patient mass that will attempt to close in the final two furlongs. This race shape strongly favours horses with proven closing ability on Good ground who can produce a sustained, linear finish rather than a sharp turn of foot, given the flat circuit at Tramore and the lack of a genuinely fierce pace to soften the leaders. The field holds far more hold-up horses than can all settle in their natural rear positions; of those pushed forward into the map's midfield, Glendower, Guy's Girl and Miss Crinshawn are most likely to end up closer to the pace than their natural style dictates.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Soaring Sun Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Soaring Sun goes forward unchallenged and Oust does not apply early pressure, the pace is controlled and moderate throughout.
scenarios.body: Soaring Sun sets a comfortable gallop and reaches the home straight with energy in reserve, kicking again when asked; the hold-up brigade face a target that simply has too much left to reel in over the relatively flat Tramore straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Wave Swamps Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely moderate and the closers time their runs well, a late surge from the massed hold-up pack overwhelms a tiring Soaring Sun.
scenarios.body: The compressed field means multiple hold-up horses arrive in a wave inside the final furlong; those with the best recent form on Good ground and a strong jockey hold the edge in the photo.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Oust Asserts from Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If Oust travels strongly just off Soaring Sun and strikes for home two furlongs out before the closers have organised themselves.
scenarios.body: Oust's youth, proximity to the pace and proven Good-ground form over 10f-13f make this achievable; Colin Keane on Forlio and Ben Coen on Miss Crinshawn would need a sharper run to get to him.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Collapse, Closers Reign
scenarios.trigger: If Soaring Sun is outpaced or stumbles early and no horse settles into a lead role, the race degenerates into a slowly-run, sprint-finish lottery.
scenarios.body: A truly compressed late dash from the rear suits only the sharpest finishers in the hold-up pack, but the low pace data and style mismatch for most closers makes a clean execution unlikely.

watchPoints.text: Soaring Sun — if she is allowed to coast in front unchallenged at a moderate tempo, she carries the whole race shape on her back; watch whether Oust or any other horse contests the lead in the first two furlongs, because any pressure transforms this from a front-runner's race to a closer's race.

Forlio — Colin Keane's booking on a horse that has quietly posted a 4th over 11f Good last time out is the single biggest jockey-upgrade flag in the race; watch for Keane positioning closer than the hold-up tag suggests as the field fans out.

Miss Crinshawn — Ben Coen on a filly with directly relevant 13f Good form, and her positional redistribution into midfield may suit her better than expected; if she travels sweetly in the first mile she becomes a live threat in the straight.

Showyoutheropes — 109 days off the track is always a risk, but Gary Carroll's record with returning horses for O'Leary and 1W/4P from 8 Good-ground runs makes this the most statistically backed closer in the field; watch market moves before the off.

A Pretty Penny — the 121lb weight advantage is one of the most significant in the field and should not be underestimated in a 1m4f Good-ground handicap; watch how she settles from the rear, as any improvement on her winning 10f form step up to 1m4f could see her outrun her odds.

races.name: August Festival Early Bird Packages On tramoreraces.ie Handicap

runners_data.name: Voice Of Reason
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner here, William Delahunty's 6-year-old gets to dictate on good ground over 2m; recent form figures of 225980 are modest and similar-going form reads 0 wins from 6, so while the tactical position is ideal the raw ability to convert it is the question.

runners_data.name: Carthusian
runners_data.note: Mrs Harrington's 4-year-old has a live trainer angle (T14: 5/34) and goes well on good ground, sitting in a natural tracking position just off the pace; headgear visor may sharpen focus and 11 days between runs is a routine gap for this yard.

runners_data.name: The Banger Doyle
runners_data.note: Veteran 10-year-old who knows his job as a prominent racer; John Queally's charge has solid good-ground form (6P in similar going) over this trip range and a 19-day break fits a horse with a busy campaign profile — consistency rather than a big win is his hallmark.

runners_data.name: Matt Connor
runners_data.note: True hold-up performer for Colin Keane, who represents a significant jockey upgrade; won over 2m on heavy and over 2m2f on good recently, suggesting the trip and ground are fine, but dependent on a pace scenario that may not materialise in this slowly-run contest.

runners_data.name: Liberated Light
runners_data.note: Returning from a remarkable 858-day absence (38 days since a comeback run), Ben Coen's mount has genuine form on good ground including a win at 2m; the tongue-tie is retained and the second run back often brings improvement, though rustiness after such a layoff is a concern.

runners_data.name: Nelson Muntz
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a 101-day break (39 since a comeback), blinkered, and ridden by 7lb claimer Jimmy Dalton for David Harry Kelly's in-form stable (T14: 2/3); best form has come with more pace to aim at and the likely steady gallop here is not ideal.

runners_data.name: Mr Rango
runners_data.note: James Barcoe's 8-year-old naturally races prominently and has a course-friendly good-ground profile; placed at 2m recently (2nd over 17f) and Siobhan Rutledge takes over, though a trainer strike-rate of 0/14 over 14 days is a cold flag.

runners_data.name: Inchiquin Maid
runners_data.note: A naturally front-running mare whose preference for racing up with the pace cannot be satisfied here given the volume of prominent types; returning from 146 days off for Terence O'Brien, she won her last start over this trip, and if she manages to secure any kind of prominent position that fitness angle is live.

runners_data.name: Master Sydney
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse for Paul Flynn shuffled into midfield on the map; the tongue-tie is on, has won over good ground, but a 48-day break and a deeply uninspiring recent form string of 04-060 makes it hard to be positive regardless of tactical position.

runners_data.name: Must Meet Cecil
runners_data.note: Cian Collins's 8-year-old is a genuine hold-up type displaced to midfield; visor applied and form reads 860 from three runs, with the best of his recent starts coming over 2m on good — but 0 wins from 12 in similar going over the distance makes him a tough recommendation.

runners_data.name: Spanish John
runners_data.note: W J Lee takes over on a horse that naturally wants to race prominently but has been mapped to midfield due to the crowded pace positions; won at 2m previously and the booking is positive, but if he cannot secure a forward pitch against his instincts the chance is compromised before a hoof is lifted.

races.paceDynamic: Voice Of Reason is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 2m handicap and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on good ground at Tramore. The prominent trio of Carthusian, The Banger Doyle and Mr Rango will look to sit just off the pace, but Spanish John and Inchiquin Maid — both natural front-runners or prominent racers — have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field holds more pace-pressing types than can all occupy their preferred position, meaning at least one of them will be shuffled back against their instincts. With Voice Of Reason setting an unhurried tempo unchallenged, this race shape is likely to be run at a steady-to-fair gallop that rewards those tracking close to the pace rather than those making up ground from the rear, as the hold-up horses will have little genuine pace injection to aim at late. The tactical verdict is clear: prominent racers who can sit just behind the leader and sustain their effort over the 2m trip are best placed; genuine hold-up horses such as Matt Connor, Liberated Light and Nelson Muntz will need an uncharacteristic injection of pace to bring their late runs into play.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Voice Of Reason dictates a measured gallop and the race is steadily run throughout, a prominent racer tracking just behind takes full advantage.
scenarios.body: Voice Of Reason sets a comfortable tempo that never truly tests the hold-up horses, and one of Carthusian, The Banger Doyle or Mr Rango, travelling smoothly in the slipstream, has enough left to assert in the straight. The good ground and flat track suit those who conserve energy by racing prominently rather than having to make up lengths against a slow pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Holds On Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Voice Of Reason gets a soft lead at a pace that suits and simply proves good enough on the day under a confident front-running ride.
scenarios.body: With no rivals able or willing to press early, Robbie Colgan can control fractions entirely on Voice Of Reason's terms, and the horse's recent 10-day turnaround suggests readiness despite modest recent form figures. On a flat track with good ground the energy saved through dictating can translate into a winning finish if the handicapper has been lenient.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough — perhaps through Spanish John or Inchiquin Maid pushing forward against type — to set up a strong late run.
scenarios.body: A contested early pace would stretch the prominent racers and bring Matt Connor, Liberated Light or Nelson Muntz into calculations, as all three have the profile and form to finish powerfully given a true gallop. Matt Connor is the most interesting of the trio given Colin Keane's booking and a recent winning run, though the steady pace scenario makes this a less likely shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Reshuffled Pacemakers
scenarios.trigger: If Spanish John or Inchiquin Maid refuses to settle mid-division and pushes forward to contest the lead, disrupting Voice Of Reason's rhythm and creating a more tactical, stop-start affair.
scenarios.body: An unsettled pace could flatten the field out and introduce uncertainty, with any horse that switches off and travels sweetly in the changing order potentially benefiting. This is the least predictable shape and the most unlikely given the field's general willingness to fill their mapped positions, but the number of naturally prominent types in the race keeps the possibility alive.

watchPoints.text: Voice Of Reason's ability to control the tempo unchallenged is the single biggest race-shaping factor — watch whether Robbie Colgan elects to stride on or dawdle, as the pace he sets will determine whether hold-up horses have any chance.

Spanish John and Inchiquin Maid are both natural front-runners pushed into midfield on the map — watch the first two furlongs for either breaking their tactical brief and pressing forward, which would fundamentally alter the race shape.

Liberated Light's 858-day absence is extreme even accounting for the 38-day comeback gap; watch how Ben Coen settles her early, as a horse returning from that layoff could over-race or fade tamely, affecting midfield traffic for others.

Matt Connor is the hold-up horse most likely to benefit if pace develops, with Colin Keane's booking a significant market signal — watch whether he can find a clear passage around the final turn given the likely bunching of the prominent horses.
Nelson Muntz's trainer David Harry Kelly is 2/3 in the last 14 days — watch the market move on this runner as stable form can translate quickly even when individual form figures are ordinary.

races.name: August Festival August 13th - 16th Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: He Who Dares
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse returning from 309 days off (4 runs for current jockey Ben Coen), with a stamina flag of fading in the finish — the long layoff and tendency to empty make him vulnerable even if the pace scenario suits.|

runners_data.name: Inchiquin Star
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up performer for Terence O'Brien who has shown placed form on good ground and over 16f trips; 299 days off is a concern, but his sim-going record (1W2P from 11) suggests the surface will not be an issue.|

runners_data.name: Cala Gracioneta
runners_data.note: Freshest horse in the race at just 4 days since last run, but that recent run was a distant 8th on good ground and the fades-in-finish flag is a recurring theme; the step back up to 2m from shorter trips is the key unknown for Matthew J Smith.|

runners_data.name: All In Peder
runners_data.note: Fitted with a hood and returning from 37 days off, this seven-year-old has a deeply modest recent record in staying handicaps — four finishes in the bottom third of the field — and the 16-18f trip range has consistently exposed him.|

runners_data.name: You Make Me Smile
runners_data.note: The race-shaper: sole front-runner who should set a controlled gallop and could be hard to peg back if the pace stays honest rather than fast; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.91) reflects this is a step up to front-running territory, but the visor and Fahy's preparation suggest intentionality.|

runners_data.name: Takarengo
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old whose genuine hold-up style cannot be fully expressed here given the glut of rear-runners — Gary Carroll will likely find himself further forward than ideal, which blunts the horse's best asset; trainer Barcoe's T14 strike rate of 1/11 offers no particular confidence.|

runners_data.name: Captain Hanley
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes a notable booking on this Colin Keane-ridden prominent racer who has placed twice over 20f on good ground; the headgear (hood/tongue-tie) angle and strong jockey upgrade make him one of the most interesting prominent types in the race.|

runners_data.name: Black Soul
runners_data.note: Carries a fades-in-finish warning alongside the redistribution note — a horse whose natural rearward style has been pushed into midfield on the map; 102 days off (24 runs for current jockey) and modest recent form on good ground make the STYLE_FIT discount (0.92) feel well-earned.|

runners_data.name: Bynx
runners_data.note: The most experienced prominent horse in the field after You Make Me Smile, with two wins and seven places from 12 good-ground runs — Martin Hassett's eight-year-old has exactly the profile to stalk the leader and strike; the 27-day freshness is a positive.|

runners_data.name: Reflectionist
runners_data.note: The extraordinary 1,518-day absence (404 runs for jockey) immediately dominates any assessment here — Gavin Cromwell is a competent handler of comeback horses but this is an extreme layoff, and the redistribution off a true hold-up style into midfield compounds the difficulty.|

runners_data.name: Synchronize
runners_data.note: Five-year-old whose best form has come over shorter trips (2nd over 13f, 4th over 16f) with a 7lb claimer aboard; the natural hold-up style is squeezed by the redistribution into midfield, and the trip looks at the outer edge of his stamina range.|

runners_data.name: Lariat
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old for Liam Cusack returning on 30 days' rest with a prominent style, but the recent form reads 0/67-7 and five runs over this trip range without a win in good ground suggest he fills the field rather than threatens it.|

races.paceDynamic: You Make Me Smile is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner 2m handicap and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, W J Lee can dictate a controlled, honest gallop on good ground without any pressure from rivals. Captain Hanley and Bynx are the other prominent-styled runners and will likely slot in directly behind, creating a small lead group with the bulk of the field strung out behind them. The redistributed hold-up horses — Takarengo, Black Soul, Reflectionist, and Synchronize — cannot all find their natural position at the rear given the volume of hold-up types in the field; in practice, some will be forced to race closer to the pace than ideal, with Takarengo and Synchronize the most likely to drift into a genuine midfield berth. A controlled single pace-setter over 2m on good ground sets up a race that will be truly run but not truly fast, meaning the finish will be about stamina and tactical acuity rather than a late sprint — the prominent profile, tracking the leader without burning energy, is ideally placed to pounce, while true hold-up horses will need something to go wrong ahead of them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If You Make Me Smile dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the prominent trackers land in the perfect stalking position.
scenarios.body: You Make Me Smile sets an honest but unhurried pace over the 2m trip and the prominent horses immediately behind drain the race of any pace injection, leaving a decisive late furlong that rewards those who have conserved energy close to the front. Captain Hanley's record at staying trips in good ground and Bynx's course form make them the most dangerous challengers to land the spoils.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop remains genuinely slow throughout and no prominent rival has the class to overhaul the leader in the straight.
scenarios.body: You Make Me Smile, with no pace pressure to knock it off its rhythm, could simply outstay the field in what becomes a test of tactical efficiency rather than raw speed. The age and headgear note (visor) suggest P A Fahy has primed this horse for exactly this sort of front-running opportunity, and a STYLE_FIT of 0.91 merely reflects the horse running at the top of its comfort zone.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough to spread the field and a genuine hold-up type finds a clear passage in the straight.
scenarios.body: He Who Dares or Inchiquin Star, both natural hold-up horses operating at the top of their OR band, could pick off a tiring field if the pace proves more searching than the single front-runner scenario suggests. The concern here is the redistribution effect — many supposed hold-up horses are not truly at the rear and may impede each other's late runs, making this outcome harder to execute than it looks on paper.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so slow that the race turns into a sprint finish where draw and position off the final bend become decisive.
scenarios.body: A truly dawdling gallop would compress the field and eliminate the advantage of any running style, turning the race into a rough-and-tumble scramble where the horse with the sharpest turn of foot wins. Synchronize showed finishing speed over shorter at Gowran and Cala Gracioneta placed over 2m on good ground, making them fringe candidates in this unlikely scenario.

watchPoints.text: Captain Hanley — Colin Keane's booking on a horse with multiple placings over 20f in good ground is the single most significant jockey-switch angle in this race; watch the market for any support that confirms the stable has him primed.

You Make Me Smile — if W J Lee allows the pace to drop to a crawl in the back straight, the field may bunch dangerously approaching the final bend, neutralising his advantage and making the outcome chaotic rather than controlled.

Takarengo and Black Soul — both genuine hold-up horses forced into midfield by the redistribution; if they attempt to switch back to their natural rear-of-field position after the start, Carroll and Roche will be fighting for the same ground in the closing stages.

Reflectionist — a 1,518-day absence is extreme even for a horse returning to a modest 0-60 handicap; monitor for any unusual behaviour in the parade ring or signs of market support that suggest Cromwell has genuinely got the horse ready.

Bynx — two wins and seven places from 12 good-ground runs is the best going-specific profile in the prominent group; if You Make Me Smile is caught, Harnett's mount is the most likely to be travelling best at the two-furlong pole.
